newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, securities inactive.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, securities inactive.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday at 9.50 to 10.00 percent, compared with the day's opening level 10.00 to 10.40 percent, dealers said.
"Market was squarish, some what easy," a primary dealer said. "Majority of deals were struck at 10 percent level."
"The higher call rates ruling at 10.00 to 10.25 levels, led to some selling pressure, mostly in the short dated securities," said Maneesh Ketkar, dealer at Ashok Leyland Investment Services.
But there was some buying in treasury bills maturing in January 1997 and February 1997 at 9.5 percent, he said.

Ketkar said the next fortnight may see call rates coming down to single digit, which may lead to increased trading activity. "The market is awaiting the 364 day treasury bills cut-off, general censensus being 10.12 percent," he said.
The trading volume on the National Stock Exchange was 735 million rupees, little lower than the previous day's 764.3 million rupees, Ketkar said.

The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Wednesday at 102.35 rupees and 102.38 rupees, down from Tuesday's level of 102.45 rupees while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock fell by 10 basis points to 102.33 rupees, dealers said.
The trasury bills maturing in November 30, 1996 were traded at 8.75 percent, dealers said.

Intercorporte deposits were quoted in the region of 17-19 percent for P1+ rated companies, while P1 rated companies were quoted in the range of 20-23 percent for 90 days, said Bharti Anand at SMIFS International Finance.
